svg.title: BCLC in brief, and the time lag
svg.desc: Schematic: the BCLC system puts tumour burden, liver function and performance status into five boxes (0 very early, A early, B intermediate, C advanced, D terminal), each linked to a first-line recommendation: stage 0, ablation or resection (resection first if transplant and surgery are both options); stage A, a choice among curative options (resection, transplant, ablation); stage B defaults to TACE but is a spectrum, not one box — limited burden (within up-to-7) may merit curative-intent options, while beyond up-to-11 TACE is strongly discouraged (Taiwan Liver Cancer Association 2025 consensus, 100% agreement); stage C, systemic therapy; stage D, best supportive care. Two footnotes: the BCLC 2022 text itself says the final decision belongs to the physician and multidisciplinary team, with treatment-stage migration built in; and for the same SBRT, APASL 2017 wrote 'not shown to improve outcomes', BCLC 2022 'further prospective studies are needed', AASLD 2023 gave it a concrete slot, and Taiwan's NHI has actually reimbursed it since 2015 (37047B) — guideline wording takes time to catch up with evidence. The 2026 BCLC update is paywalled; this figure follows the 2022 version.

g.text: BCLC — MAP, NOT VERDICT
BCLC in brief, and the time lag
BCLC puts tumour burden × liver function × performance status into five boxes,
each with a first-line recommendation. The two footnotes below are what patients rarely get shown.
0 · very early
Single small lesion, preserved liver
Ablation or resection; resection first if transplant and surgery are both options (BCLC 2022)
A · early
Single or a few nodules, liver-confined
Choose among curative options — resection / transplant / ablation, by liver function and tumour
B · intermediate
Multinodular, liver-confined
TACE by default — but stage B is a spectrum, not one box (TLCA 2025, 100% agreement)
Limited burden (within up-to-7): curative-intent options may be feasible
Beyond up-to-11: TACE strongly discouraged — systemic therapy
C · advanced
Vascular invasion or spread
Systemic therapy leads
D · terminal
Decompensated liver, poor status
Best supportive care leads; individual cases judged by the team
In the map's own words (BCLC 2022)
The final decision must be taken by the responsible physician and tumour board; decisions should not rest on a simplified figure alone.
Treatment-stage migration is built in: individual factors can legitimately shift the advice to a 'later-stage' treatment — the stage stays, the road moves.
The time lag between guidelines and evidence — the same SBRT, four wordings
APASL 2017: 'not shown to improve outcomes' (grade C2) | BCLC 2022: 'bears antitumoral activity but further prospective studies are needed'
AASLD 2023: a concrete slot (not amenable to ablation; central or perivascular) | Taiwan NHI: actually reimbursed since February 2015 (37047B)
What separates these is not the evidence flipping — it is how long convention takes to catch up: 'delayed acceptance' (Moon 2026).
The 2026 BCLC update is published but paywalled — this figure follows the 2022 version.
Schematic, redrawn from BCLC 2022 (Reig), the TLCA 2025 intermediate-stage consensus, APASL 2017, AASLD 2023,
Moon 2026 and the Taiwan NHI 37047B criteria
